Process industries run on continuous physics: yields, energy and safety windows decided by process telemetry. Advanced process control plus predictive maintenance plus energy intelligence is the classic compounding stack — now with agentic planning on top.

items: SIS/DCS estates face convergence threats with physical consequence; IEC 62443 incomplete.
APC setpoints static while feedstock shifts; yield and energy losses accepted as normal.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Identity & Access Modernization, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Cloud Security & Posture Management from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (APC/advanced control, Predictive maintenance, Batch genealogy/investigation) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — IEC 62443 / ISA S84 among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Manufacturing & Industrial level this capability reads as: restoration-tested backups and manual-fallback procedures for production lines (recovery time proven in drills). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
